observedTimelineUtc.event: Android clearApplicationUserData/force stop begins; prior application data cleared for the test.
One 5000 ms process-lock acquisition warning while Maestro is still entering the synthetic email, before sign-in.

establishedFindings.finding: The application uses the official processLock and does not override lockAcquireTimeout. The pinned Auth SDK default is 5000 ms.

The pinned SDK processLock clears its acquisition timer after successful acquisition and on its error path. The warning occurs in the timeout callback before ProcessLockAcquireTimeoutError is rejected. A harmless uncleared success timer is not supported by this source.

authStore registers a synchronous onAuthStateChange callback. Auth/profile/push work triggered by noninitial events is deferred via setTimeout. INITIAL_SESSION resolves a promise and returns. No direct awaited Supabase call is present inside this callback.
The inspected production-mobile source has one createClient call. This source observation does not prove a runtime instance count.
The failing UI run uses the actual SDK and AsyncStorage, with synthetic HTTP/Realtime transports. The fixture starts with owner=null, offline=false and delayMs=0; it does not seed an auth session.

The run later signs in a synthetic actor and performs profile/feed requests. Its demonstrated Home assertion blocker is the Android microphone prompt; the warning alone does not identify a persistent auth deadlock or a production outage.

unknowns: The log does not record which auth operation held the lock, which operation waited, acquisition/release spans, storage read durations or runtime client instance IDs.
No instrumented native reproduction establishes whether the wait arose from startup storage scheduling, queued SDK work or another runtime condition.
A local Node fixture would not establish Hermes/Android scheduling behavior; none is substituted for native reproduction.
recommendedBoundedNextStep: On a disposable QA emulator rerun, add timing-only observation around the unchanged processLock callback and AsyncStorage operations, including a locally generated client instance label and operation ID. Record acquisition/hold/release timing and error class without tokens, sessions, user identifiers, raw payloads or keys. Do not change timeout, bypass locking or suppress the warning. Implement only after coordination with root.
